newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund vol dips, gilt vols show late rally.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund vol dips, gilt vols show late rally.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE drifted off on Wednesday, while gilt volatility showed a late rally ahead of the election on Thursday, traders said.

However, traders said gilt options activity had now died down, as most investors were happy with their positioning and Bund vol was unlikely to fall much further ahead of the key non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
"Bund vol looks cheap given the importance of Friday's data," said a salesman at a European bank in London. "There's reasonable flow in gilts, with sporadic call activity."

Gilt volatility showed a late spurt, heading to 8.5 percent compared with 8.0 percent earlier in the week, but traders said it was still low compared with the 10.5 percent level seen in 1992, when the last election was held.
June gilt futures were up 19/32 at 110-09 by 1430 GMT.
More than 16,000 June calls were traded at strikes from 108-00 to 114-00, while just under 7,000 puts were traded between 107-00 and 110-00.
June Bund futures were unchanged at 100.97 by 1430 GMT.
June options volatility was at 5.35 to 5.45 percent, compared with 5.55 to 5.65 percent at the open.
A trader at a French bank here said he advised caution ahead of the U.S. data, despite a generally optimistic tone in the market. He advised buying volatility on dips.

"There was an over-reaction to yesterday's (US) employment cost index, which people took to mean that there is no inflationary pressure," said a trader at French bank here. "But after all, it is only one piece of data, and the non-farms could easily cause a shock."
